articles.title: El número uno cambia de manos, no de país
articles.standfirst: Andrea Revuelta coge el testigo de Paula Martín y se proclama número uno mundial amateur
articles.summary: Andrea Revuelta coge el testigo de Paula Martín y se proclama número uno mundial amateur
articles.body: ''No nos vamos a ir en un futuro muy lejano'' decía Andrea Revuelta porque el golf español viene para quedarse. Hace una semana, el 26 de septiembre, Paula Martín se coronaba como número uno del mundo en el World Amateur Golf Ranking (WAGR) tras el paso al profesionalismo de Kiara Romero. Pero lo realmente histórico es que Andrea Revuelta la seguía muy de cerca en segundo lugar. Por primera vez en la historia del golf español, en el oro y la plata del ranking mundial figuraban nombres nacionales. En 2024, la malagueña Julia López consiguió el título de número uno. Dos años después, España vuelve a tener representantes en el podio mundial amateur. Las jugadoras madrileñas no solo comparten amistad sino también comparten un lista muy larga de participaciones conjuntas. Ambas fueron jugadoras del programa CETEMA de la Real Federación de Golf de Madrid, han representado a los equipos nacionales de la Real Federación Española de Golf en múltiples competiciones y ahora comparten universidad pues están en Stanford compaginando su carrera deportiva y académica. Esta semana, el nombre de número uno ha quedado en manos de Andrea Revuelta que, tan solo una semana después, ha dado relevo a su compatriota Paula Martín. La jugadora de la Real Sociedad Hípica Española consta de un amplio palmarés de victorias como el Campeonato de España Absoluto de 2023 y 2024, la Copa S.M la Reina de 2024 y dos victorias en Estados Unidos. Además, la joven de 20 años anota dos recientes segundos puestos en los prestigiosos The Women's Amateur Championship disputado en Escocia y el Augusta National Women's Amateur. Revuelta reflexionaba sobre su evolución y su juego en los últimos años. ''Yo creo que estar en América me ha ayudado mucho con el nivel de juego, la exigencia y la competición incrementa mucho'' explicaba. ''Mi universidad es un ambiente mucho más competitivo que lo que había aquí en España''. La madrileña destacaba la progresión gradual en su juego, lo que le ha permitido mejorar y adaptarse a los retos a los que se ha enfrentado. ''Siempre he querido mejorar y siempre estoy cambiando y mejorando cosas'' afirmaba la joven. ''A lo mejor te puedo decir que he notado más cambio desde que puse mucho más énfasis en el trabajo mental que en otras partes''. Los deportista más destacados de nuestro país se caracterizan por el aspecto mental luchador. En este deporte, muchos profesionales han reiterado la importancia del aspecto mental en el rendimiento de los jugadores de élite, representando así el 80% del juego según Jack Nicklaus. Con dos años de universidad por delante, la madrileña planea dar su paso al profesionalismo al termino de su carrera universitaria. El hito de la élite amateur se convierte en normalidad para Andrea Revuelta que comienza el año académico con humildad y los objetivos claros. ''En mi día a día tengo que seguir mejorando y tratarlo como un hito, pero hasta cierto punto porque sé que puedo dar más de mí'' comentaba Revuelta. ''Una cosa que me ha enseñado la universidad es que si has llegado hasta un punto haciendo lo que haces, no tienes que cambiar o hacer nada nuevo''. La madrileña lleva años consolidada en el top mundial pero en los dos últimos años su juego la ha llevado hasta el liderato. ''Me ayuda muchísimo rodearme de gente que es mejor que yo, por eso he mejorado tanto en Estados Unidos'' consideraba tras mencionar los subcampeonatos en el Augusta National Women's Amateur y en el Women's Amateur Championship. ''Me he rodeado de gente que es mejor que yo y eso te hace querer ser mejor y puedes aprender muchísimo''.

articles.title: Tiger Woods' Son Charlie Announces TaylorMade Endorsement Contract in New Video
articles.summary: Charlie Woods has joined the same company as his father.
articles.body:
Charlie Woods has joined the same company as his father.

TaylorMade announced Friday that Charlie Woods, the son of legendary golfer Tiger Woods, has signed an endorsement deal with the company.

First look at Pro Bowler coaching for CFB team

The elder Woods began his equipment partnership with TaylorMade in 2017, and he launched his "Sun Day Red" brand with the company in 2024 following his split with Nike, who was his sponsor for more than two decades.

The younger Woods has obviously been in the spotlight for his entire life because of his father's status as one of the best golfers in the world, but he's begun forging quite a career of his own.

In 2020, he became the youngest competitor in the PNC Championships at age 11, and he's since gone on to participate in a number of other high-level events.

Last summer, he won a three-way playoff at the Eagle Trace Golf Club qualifier to make the U.S. Junior Amateur. He participated in the U.S. Junior Amateur Championship this summer until he was eliminated in late July.

The 17-year-old Woods is heading into his senior season of high school and is committed to play collegiate golf for Florida State, keeping him in his home state as he takes the next step in his career.

Woods has big shoes to fill, being the son of an all-time great, but his career has gotten off to a solid start.

articles.title: DP World Tour Golf: Thriston Lawrence leads at halfway stage of Omega European Masters as he aims to emulate Seve Ballesteros
articles.summary: England's Harry Hall marches up leaderboard before injury sees him bogey three of his final five holes; Hall's countryman Paul Casey four shots behind Thriston Lawrence, who is looking to equal Seve Ballesteros by winning this event for third time since it joined DP World Tour schedule
articles.body:
Ballesteros is the only player to win this event three times since it became a DP World Tour tournament in 1972, doing so in 1977, 1978 and 1989 - but Lawrence has a chance to do likewise having triumphed at Crans-sur-Siere in 2022 and then again last season.

The South African carded a bogey-free, seven-under 63 on Friday to reach 13 under par and take a two-shot advantage over Germany's Jeremy Paul and Spain's Ignacio Elvira - who shot a round-of-the day 62 - into the weekend in Switzerland.

Japan's Keita Nakajima sits fourth on 10 under with England's Paul Casey among a group of three players in a share of fifth on nine under with 36 holes remaining.

Casey's compatriot Harry Hall reached 10 under through nine holes of his second round after five front-nine birdies saw him go out in 30, only for a hip injury to then hamper him as he bogeyed three of his final five and slipped to seven under, six shots off the pace.

Lawrence: I've been playing well all year

Starting at the 10th, Lawrence parred five of his first six holes around a birdie at 13 before he ignited from the 16th when a superb tee shot left him a tap-in birdie.

The 29-year-old picked up shots at his next five holes, too, with highlights including draining from over 40 feet at the first and then holing from off the green at the second.

Lawrence was unable to add to his birdie haul across the last third of his round but saved par at five when he chipped on from the sand - his second attempt to get out of that hazard having initially used the putter to no avail.

Lawrence, without a top-10 finish since March, said afterwards: "I've played well all year. I've just been unfortunate so many times, missing the cut by one shot four or five times. I feel like I've been playing well, but mentally, I'm in a much better space.

"Obviously, seeing birdies and seeing putts go in, I feel like you gain confidence from that. Coming back to a place I love is just extra confidence."

Paul shot a six-under 64 in round two, with six birdies and an eagle - five of which came on his back nine, including a gain at the last - around bogeys at seven and nine.

Elvira, one of four runners-up to Joe Dean at last week's British Masters at The Belfry, mixed nine birdies with a solitary bogey in his eight-under Friday, chipping in for gains at the third and the ninth during his lowest round on the DP World Tour since July 2023. articles.title: Predicting the NFC North: Vikings, Bears, Lions leave Packers in the dust
articles.summary: We ranked each position group, assigned points, and predicted the final 2026 NFC North standings.
articles.body:
Have you recently scanned the rosters of the teams in the NFC North? Three of them are stacked on both sides of the ball, while the cheeseheads in Green Bay leave a lot to be desired.

It really does look like a three-horse race in the North. Green Bay has a solid foundation with quarterback Jordan Love, but who is going to help him move the ball on offense? Josh Jacobs is on the NFL's exempt list amid legal accusations, and the receiver room is filled with guys who haven't been able to stay healthy.

Defensively, Micah Parsons is on the Physically Unable to Perform list, and the Packers are likely combating the elite wideouts of the North with Keisean Nixon and rookie Brandon Cisse as their top two cornerbacks. Good luck with that.

I have the Vikings finishing 14-3 this season . It might be overly optimistic, but the defense is legit, and Kevin O'Connell's offenses have been dynamic when the quarterback play is above average. Look no further than the 13-win team in 2022 and the 14-win team in 2024.

As good as I think the Vikings are, I don't think the Bears and Lions are far behind. To help tell the story, I've ranked each team by position group (4 points for first place, 3 for second place, and so on). You'll notice that Green Bay comes in last five times. That, folks, is a recipe for disaster.

Yeah, I think Kyler Murray is better than Jordan Love. Jared Goff is terrific when given time to throw to his skill guys, but Caleb Williams is a potential MVP candidate this season.

Jahmyr Gibbs might put up prime LaDainian Tomlinson-like numbers for Detroit, while Aaron Jones and Jordan Mason give Minnesota a strong 1a and 1b at running back.

The Bears are right behind Minnesota with D'Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai.

Green Bay, with the unproven Marshawn Lloyd as their No. 1 back until Jacobs returns (which isn't a guarantee), could be in serious trouble.

Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison, and Jauan Jennings give Minnesota the best WR trio in the NFL. If T.J. Hockenson can regain his form from two years ago, the Vikings will be impossible to slow down.

Detroit is nearly as loaded with Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams, and Sam LaPorta.

The Bears, with Rome Odunze and Luther Burden, have upside but a lot to prove at receiver. Colston Loveland could be one of the most productive tight ends in the NFL.

The Packers boast Christian Watson, Jayden Reed, and Matthew Golden at receiver, and Tucker Kraft, who has to prove himself at tight end after suffering a torn ACL last November. Watson, who had 35 receptions last season, is their leading returning receiver.

Chicago should be strong again with Braxton Jones, Joe Thuney, Garrett Bradbury, Jonah Jackson, and Darnell Wright up front. Bradbury gave Minnesota fans nightmares for years, but he's been really good since leaving the Vikings.

Minnesota could leap to No. 1 in this category if they stay healthy. Christian Darrisaw has to prove that he's as good as he was pre-2024 knee injury, and that's the biggest key to the line this season. Donovan Jackson might be a mauler in Year 2 at left guard, while Will Fries and Brian O'Neill can dominate the right side. If Blake Brandel can handle starting at center, the Vikings will be in good shape.

Penei Sewell moves from right tackle to left tackle, and rookie Blake Miller is starting at right tackle for the Lions. The middle features Christian Mahogany, Juice Scruggs, and Tate Ratledge. It could be good, but a lot depends on Ratledge and Miller on the right side.

The Packers are in trouble unless Jordan Morgan and Aaron Banks are good at left tackle and left guard, respectively. PFF ranks Green Bay's line 28th going into the season, which is another reason their offense could struggle to score points.

Detroit is menacing with Aidan Hutchinson, and they have decent options behind him on the edge in 2025 second-round pick Derrick Moore and former Viking D.J. Wonnum. Tyleik Williams, their 2025 first-round pick, and Alim McNeill are a nice 1-2 punch on the D-line.

Dallas Turner might lead the league in sacks if the preseason hype about him is real. That makes Minnesota even more dangerous, especially with Andrew Van Ginkel and newly signed edge rusher Kyle Van Noy in the mix. Up front, Jalen Redmond blossomed into a stud last season, while rookies Caleb Banks and Domonique Orange have a chance to make the Vikings elite.

Green Bay gets a lower profile here because Parsons is starting the season on the PUP list. While he's out, it's up to Lukas Van Ness and the little-known Barryn Sorrell to bring pressure. At D-tackle, Devonte Wyatt is a stud.

Chicago's pass rush is led by Montez Sweat, but there isn't a lot behind him off the edge. Austin Booker has to make a jump to give them more pass-rushing juice. On the D-line, past-his-prime Grady Jarrett and Neville Gallimore are projected to start after the Bears traded Gervon Dexter. That ain't great.

I like the Bears with Devin Bush alongside T.J. Edwards. That's arguably two of the 25 best inside linebackers in the league.

I really like Green Bay's starters with Edgerrin Cooper and Zaire Franklin, but only if Franklin can return to his pre-2025 form. Last year, he posted a career-worst 38.0 PFF grade.

Detroit might have the best inside linebacker in the division with Jack Campbell, but Malcolm Rodriguez and Derrick Barnes have more to prove, in my opinion.

The Vikings are last in this category, but that doesn't mean they're bad. It's just a product of the other teams having really strong inside linebackers. Blake Cashman and Eric Wilson are solid starters, and Minnesota has no reason to worry with them on the field.

Chicago has a fairly high-end duo at cornerback with Jaylon Johnson and Tyrique Stevenson. They'll be even stronger if Kyler Gordon returns from the PUP list.

I like the Vikings by a hair over Detroit with the trio of Byron Murphy Jr., Isaiah Rodgers, and James Pierre. Rookie Chuck Demmings might jump Pierre for playing time, but that's a good problem to have.

Detroit signing D.J. Reed gives them a shutdown corner to pair with Rock Ya-Sin, who is a serviceable No. 2 cornerback. Keith Abney at nickel could be good, but he's a rookie who has yet to prove anything against NFL talent.

Green Bay is in trouble here. Keisean Nixon and rookie second-round pick Brandon Cisse as the top two corners is a problem, especially if Cisse isn't a star.

Xavier McKinney and Evan Williams are an elite safety duo, and the Packers are going to need them to play at their highest level yet because of the concerns at cornerback.

Chicago looked great with Coby Bryant and first-round pick Dillon Thieneman at safety, but Bryant's season is likely over after undergoing knee surgery. That leaves the rookie and Xavier Woods as the starters, and that could be problematic.

The Vikings could be fine if Harrison Smith returns. Then they could pair him and Josh Metellus with Jay Ward, Theo Jackson, Jakobe Thomas, and Jacob Thomas rounding out the depth.

Detroit could jump to the top of this list if Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph eventually return from injury, but right now they're last with projected starters Avonte Maddux and Chuck Clark.

Special teams: Vikings, Bears, Lions, Packers

This is a big deal. Minnesota has the best kicker in Will Reichard, and rookie punter Brett Thorson performed very well in the preseason. With Myles Price being a dynamic return man, the Vikings are in good shape.

Tory Taylor gives the Bears an elite punter, and Cairo Santos is decent enough as a veteran kicker. Adding Kalif Raymond, who spent the past five seasons in Detroit, as an elite return man could swing games in Chicago's favor.

Detroit has a solid kicker/punter duo with Jack Bates and Jack Fox, while the return game is TBD with Tom Kennedy, Jacob Saylors, and Jabari Small.

Green Bay has a terrific punter in Daniel Whalen, but putting games on the foot of rookie sixth-round kicker Trey Smack is risky business. I do like Skyy Moore as a reliable kick and punt returner for the Packers.

If I award 4 points for a first-place ranking, 3 points for second, 2 points for third, and 1 point for fourth in my position group rankings, the Bears win the tally with 27 total points, followed by the Vikings (25), Lions (23), and Packers (15).

But that doesn't necessarily equate to wins. The schedule matters, and Minnesota plays an easier schedule than Chicago (but not Detroit). That plays into my 14-3 prediction for the Vikings, which includes road losses to Chicago, Detroit, and New England.

Minnesota wins the NFC North outright. But how far behind will the Bears, Lions and Packers be?

I honestly believe the Bears and Lions will both finish 11-6 and find a spot in the playoffs.

What about Green Bay? Their season will spiral out of control during a brutal mid-season stretch of games against Tampa Bay, Chicago, Dallas, Detroit, Carolina, New England, Minnesota, and the L.A. Rams. They might lose six or seven of those.

When it's all said and done, Green Bay will be staring up at everyone else with a 5-12 record.

articles.title: LIV Golf Embarrassment Continues at DP World Tour Q-School
articles.summary: As LIV Golf’s future remains uncertain, professional golfer Peter Uihlein entered to compete in the DP World Tour Q-School, but he failed to show up to his t...
articles.body:
As LIV Golf's future remains uncertain, professional golfer Peter Uihlein entered to compete in the DP World Tour Q-School, but he failed to show up to his third round tee-time. He started the event poorly, shooting a 74 and a 73 in the first two rounds respectively. When he was not at the tee on Friday, the event disqualified him off the leaderboard. Prior to his disqualification, he stood at 66th place and required a 19th place finish at least to advance further in the competition.

Many of those involved with LIV Golf like Uihlein are still awaiting news about their future. They need to plan contingencies unless LIV Golf 2.0, the next stage of the startup, fails to launch. Fellow LIV Golfers Luis Masaveu and Jose Luis Ballester are also participating in the event to qualify for DP World Tour status.

Uihlein experienced a mini-career resurgence on LIV Golf after several years of struggle on the PGA Tour. He lost his tour card during the 2020 season before gaining it again with a Korn Ferry Tour win in 2021. In the 2022 season, Uihlein missed eight cuts on the PGA Tour before being one of the first golfers to join LIV Golf. He had three top fives and two top tens on LIV his first season. 2023 and 2024 showcased his continued improvements with 22 top 20 finishes and two wins on the Asian Tour.

LIV Golf's Peter Uihlein Disqualified at DP World Tour Q-School

In 2022, Uihlein was asked about his experience on the PGA Tour, and he responded with a tone of regret.

He said, "In reality is I wish I played better. I'm not denying that."

However, the golfer also displayed relief about a fresh start with a new golf league.

"I've always kind of done things differently. I feel better. I feel freer. I feel happier… then the reality is, this is the first time in my entire career I've had a guaranteed place to play for the next year or the following year. I've never had that in my career. I don't know if that's another reason but I've never experienced that."

DP World Tour Q-School Offers Second Life For Professional Golfers

The final stage of DP World Tour Q-School will take place in Spain from November 6th to 11th. It is a six round contest where the top 15 players earn their DP World Tour cards for the 2027 season. For someone like Luis-Ballester, a young player with plenty of talent, an opportunity on the DP World Tour could help him in the long run. As far as we know, the PGA Tour has no interest in giving a helping hand to those involved with LIV Golf any further. Luis-Ballester would have to earn his way onto the PGA Tour through the DP World Tour. Whatever happens with LIV Golf, how the players from the league move forward will be fascinating to follow at an individual level.
